subject: Helios Hosted -> Dedicated: landing ops & scaling acceptance runway
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Roy <sana@helioshealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helios Procurement <procurement@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T08:14:00Z
Subject: Helios hosted->dedicated: proposed landing ops + preflight windows

Hi Sana / team,

Great to speak yesterday — following up with a concrete ops runway for the hosted->dedicated move tied to HLS-2042. Attaching the capacity report we ran against Helios traffic samples (capacity_report_v1.pdf). High-level proposal below: 

- Preflight week (non-prod canary): Mon 2026-06-22 -> Fri 2026-06-26 — validate throughput at 80% sustained load, KV cache warmup, and latency SLAs.
- Staged cutover (prod): Weekend maintenance window Sat 2026-07-03 02:00-07:00 UTC — reserve rollback window until 2026-07-05 18:00 UTC.
- Post-cutover ramp: 72-hour gradual ramp to full traffic with automatic throttles/observability gates.

Asks for Helios: please confirm procurement timeline for the dedicated commitment and whether the 2026-07-03 window works for your operations team. We also need a primary on-call for the preflight days and a provisioning ok from your security/compliance reviewer.

Attachments: capacity_report_v1.pdf (sample traffic sims + sizing), baseline latency histogram.

Next steps: Marcus and Monica will validate the acceptance checklist items and return the runbook stub by EOD 2026-06-12. Sana, if procurement can sign by 2026-06-18 we can hold the cutover window.

Thanks,
Mateo
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
[attachment: capacity_report_v1.pdf (pdf)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Sana Roy <sana@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Helios hosted->dedicated: proposed landing ops + preflight windows

Thanks — quick technical notes from the runtime/serving side (see attached sim output).

- Throughput check: the sample profile shows many short requests (median 120 tokens) with 10% of spikes to 1k tokens. For safe acceptance we should validate sustained 85% of the projected p95 RPS for a 30-minute window during preflight.
- KV cache: we recommend pre-warming the top-50 prefixes and verifying cold-start tail latency. See kv-cache-estimate.txt for the estimated warmup time (approx 11–14 minutes under our continuous batching).
- Quantization/variant fallback: we'll serve quantized v1 for cost predictability with a fallback unquantized variant in another AZ for 48 hours post-cutover.

Proposed acceptance gates (required to mark preflight as PASS):
  * p95 latency under 220ms for 95% of samples during a 30-minute load-run
  * No degradations in response correctness on a 30-case prompt suite (we'll run the eval harness)
  * No >1% increase in token cost above modeled baseline

Attachments: throughput-sim.csv, kv-cache-estimate.txt

I'll prepare the runbook skeleton and drop it in Drive by EOD 2026-06-12.

- Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: throughput-sim.csv]

Appreciate the clear plan. Two quick items from my side: procurement is lining up to sign the commitment by 2026-06-18 — I pushed for the shortened approval path and procurement confirmed the DocuSign will be routed this week.
